axes.name: Hue family
axes.what_it_measures: OKLCH hue angle h (degrees, 0-360) of the skin's identity accent, i.e. the angle of the (a,b) vector in Oklab.

axes.name: Chroma floor
axes.what_it_measures: OKLCH chroma C of the identity accent: the radius from the neutral axis, i.e. how much hue the colour actually carries.
axes.rule: If C < 0.04 the accent is achromatic and the hue axis is not evaluated; otherwise the hue axis decides. C is not otherwise used to split categories.

categories.title: Red
categories.definition: Red-family accents from the magenta/red boundary to the red/orange boundary, covering pure red and its crimson and vermilion neighbours.
categories.rationale: 11 skins, identity-accent h 8.0-39.5, median C 0.181, median L 0.581. Anchored by CSS red (h 29.2) and crimson (h 20.1); the band closes just past orangered (35.4) at the 39.5/50.8 density minimum.

categories.title: Orange
categories.definition: The red-orange band between the red and amber cuts, where terracotta, sienna and chocolate hues sit.
categories.rationale: 5 skins, h 50.8-54.9, median C 0.123, median L 0.660. Anchored by chocolate (50.3) and saddlebrown (50.8); the band is narrow because the catalogue is thin between coral (40.2) and darkorange (58.3).

categories.title: Amber
categories.definition: The yellow-orange band from darkorange to goldenrod: amber, brass, cream and warm-paper accents.
categories.rationale: 16 skins, h 62.0-86.2, median C 0.119, median L 0.770 - the second-largest cell. CSS orange (70.7) and goldenrod (84.0) both land here; the label 'amber' is chosen because it names the family more precisely than 'orange' at this hue. CSS has no 'amber' keyword; the anchors are orange (70.7) and goldenrod (84.0).

categories.title: Yellow
categories.definition: The yellow band from gold through pure yellow and olive.
categories.rationale: 5 skins, h 90.5-109.8, median C 0.145, median L 0.820. Anchored by gold (95.3), khaki (102.8) and yellow/olive (109.8).

categories.title: Green
categories.definition: The green band from chartreuse through pure green to spring green, including sage and forest tints.
categories.rationale: 8 skins, h 125.8-152.4, median C 0.118, median L 0.742. Anchored by yellowgreen (126.6), chartreuse (136.0) and green (142.5).

categories.title: Jade
categories.definition: The blue-green band between spring green and the teal cut: mint, seafoam and jade accents.
categories.rationale: 3 skins, h 161.8-168.0, median C 0.081, median L 0.862. Anchored by mediumspringgreen (156.9) and aquamarine (169.0); this cell is separated from teal by a 20.0-degree empty interval, one of the widest in the catalogue. No CSS keyword sits at this hue; the anchors are mediumspringgreen (156.9) and aquamarine (169.0).

categories.title: Teal
categories.definition: The teal band centred on the cyan/teal hue.
categories.rationale: 2 skins, h 188.0-195.1, median C 0.118, median L 0.777. CSS teal and cyan are both h 194.8. Thin cell: the catalogue has only two accents here.

categories.title: Azure
categories.definition: Cyan-leaning blues between teal and true blue.
categories.rationale: 2 skins, h 209.8-217.2, median C 0.106, median L 0.739. Anchored by powderblue (205.7) and lightblue (219.7). Thin cell. CSS 'azure' itself is a pale cyan at h 196.9 and is not the anchor - the name labels the cyan-leaning blues anchored by powderblue/lightblue/skyblue.

categories.title: Blue
categories.definition: The blue band from deep sky blue through pure blue to midnight blue.
categories.rationale: 28 skins, h 237.3-266.1, median C 0.126, median L 0.544 - the largest cell by far (26% of the catalogue). Anchored by deepskyblue (231.6), blue (264.1) and midnightblue (272.8).

categories.title: Violet
categories.definition: The violet band from slate blue and indigo to dark orchid.
categories.rationale: 10 skins, h 286.3-311.4, median C 0.135, median L 0.647. Anchored by slateblue (285.5), blueviolet (301.4) and darkorchid (311.5).

categories.title: Magenta
categories.definition: The magenta/rose band from violet through magenta to pink, wrapping across 0 degrees.
categories.rationale: 8 skins, identity-accent h 328.4-357.5, median C 0.186, median L 0.690. Anchored by violet (327.2), magenta (328.4), hotpink (352.0) and pink (7.1). This is the only category whose interval wraps 0 degrees.

categories.title: Achromatic
categories.definition: Accents with no usable hue: greys, off-whites and near-neutrals below the chroma floor.
categories.rationale: 11 skins, median C 0.024, median L 0.578. Nine of the eleven are named as neutrals (mono, obsidian, graphite, steel-thread, bone-white, liquid-silver, minimal-graphite, dark-bone, warm-ash); the other two (sisyphus, warm-parchment) are near-neutral by measurement. Hue is powerless in this cell by the CSS Color 4 rule.

hard_calls.why: The name describes the shell (#F7F6FA, C 0.007). The accent is #7CA1FA at h 266 / C 0.145, a periwinkle blue, so the accent rule says blue. A shell-based rule would say achromatic; the taxonomy measures the accent.
Accent h 256 / C 0.110 is a sky blue, about 35 deg from the jade centroid; 'aurora' is thematic, not chromatic. Kept blue.
Accent #AA3602 is rust at C 0.217; 'concrete' names the wall. Kept red.

h 65.4 sits 6.9 deg inside amber, between CSS darkorange (58.3) and orange (70.7). The character is orange-amber; the cut puts it in amber. It is the first skin that would move if the orange/amber cut moved to about 65.
Accent #A53065 is a deep rose (C 0.218); 'chrome' and 'rain' are surface metaphors. Kept magenta.
The authored light accent is a slate blue (h 253, C 0.107), 2.7x the chroma floor; charcoal describes the shell. Blue is the measured accent - a shell-based taxonomy would call it achromatic.

The dark palette is a red wall (#200608) with a gold accent (#E8B84A, h 84.9). 'Crimson' names the wall; the accent is amber. This is the weakest result in the catalogue and the clearest argument for a future shell-aware revision.
Accent h 289.8 / C 0.126 is violet; obsidian names the black shell. Kept violet.
h 86.2 is 2.18 deg below the amber/yellow cut - the closest skin to any boundary. Chroma is low (0.088), so the hue reads less strongly than the name suggests.
Identity accent is the light one at h 23.1 (C 0.080), a crimson rose. The nearest named reference is crimson (20.1), not magenta, so red.
Accent #C8B040 is olive-gold at h 97, 45 deg from the green anchor; the forest is in the shell. Kept yellow.
Accent #8B80E8 is periwinkle at h 286.3 / C 0.151 - violet, not navy. 'Midnight' is a mood word. Kept violet.
h 195.1 is CSS teal (194.8) to within 0.3 deg. The name reads blue, the measurement does not.

Two-identity skin: the authored light accent is sepia (#8E623A, h 62) and the dark accent is grey (C 0.036). The rule takes the authored light accent (dark is derived), giving amber. A dark-mode-first user would call it achromatic.
Identity accent is the light one at h 39.5 / C 0.150 - coral (CSS coral is 40.2), 5.7 deg inside red. Peach reads orange; at this hue it is a coral red.
The accent is vermilion (h 25.9, C 0.190) on cream paper; the paper is the shell. Kept red.
Accent h 39.5 / C 0.173 is coral red, 5.7 deg from the cut. Sun imagery reads orange, the hue is red-side.
Identity accent is the light one at h 8.0 / C 0.135 - a deep pink red, 5.2 deg from the magenta cut and 37 deg from orange. Sunset reads orange; the measurement does not.
Accent h 340.5 / C 0.228 is hot pink; 'sunset' is thematic. Kept magenta.
Accent h 50.9 is terracotta (CSS chocolate is 50.3), 5.7 deg inside orange. 'Warm' does not separate orange from amber.
The authored light accent has C 0.0365, 0.0035 under the chroma floor; the dark accent has C 0.060. The skin straddles the gate - at a floor of 0.03 it would be orange.
Accent is #FFFF00, pure yellow at C 0.211; the name describes a flash of light, not a hue. Kept yellow.

unverified: The chroma floor C < 0.04 is ASSERTED, not sourced. No peer-reviewed OKLCH chroma JND value was retrieved. 0.04 sits in the largest gap of the low-chroma tail (0.0383 to 0.0420) but that gap is only 0.0037 wide. A forced-choice hue-naming experiment at C 0.02-0.06 on the product's actual dark shells would settle it.

The number of hue sectors (11) is a product constraint - 12 chips minus one achromatic cell - not a result derived from colour science. At 10 or 12 chromatic sectors some cut falls inside an occupied cluster.

Category names are English colour words, not a controlled vocabulary; mapping a word to an OKLCH interval is conventional. In particular the 'amber' cell contains CSS orange (h 70.7), and the 45.2-58.5 cell could be called terracotta rather than orange.

The identity-accent rule (authored mode first, then higher chroma) was chosen on principle; it was not validated against observer data. Using the light accent unconditionally would move 14 of 109 skins.

'Name implies' labels are my own reading of the 74 skin names that carry a colour word; 35 names make no colour claim and are excluded from the agreement test, so 70% agreement is a lower bound on nothing in particular.
No observer study, no naming-agreement survey, and no perceptual validation were run for this document.
